title: My Love (Paul McCartney and Wings song)

sections.heading: Lead
Background and composition
Recording
sections.wikitext:
McCartney invited [[Richard Anthony Hewson|Richard Hewson]], with whom he had worked before while with the Beatles, to arrange the orchestral accompaniment for "My Love".{{cite web |last=Eder |first=Bruce |url=https://www.AllMusic.com/artist/richard-hewson-mn0001084923/biography |title=Richard Hewson |publisher=[[AllMusic]] |access-date=4 March 2018 |archive-date=5 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180305063952/https://www.allmusic.com/artist/richard-hewson-mn0001084923/biography |url-status=live }} The song was recorded live at [[Abbey Road Studios]] in London{{sfn|Doyle|2013|pp=82–83}} with a 50-piece orchestra accompanying the band.{{cite web |last=Breihan |first=Tom |url=https://www.stereogum.com/2037458/the-number-ones-paul-mccartney-wings-my-love/franchises/the-number-ones/ |title=The Number Ones: Paul McCartney & Wings' 'My Love' |website=[[Stereogum]] |date=8 April 2019 |access-date=27 April 2019 |archive-date=9 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190409132323/https://www.stereogum.com/2037458/the-number-ones-paul-mccartney-wings-my-love/franchises/the-number-ones/ |url-status=live }} The session took place in January 1973, late in the recording for Wings' second album, ''[[Red Rose Speedway]]''.{{sfn|Perasi|2013|pp=85, 86}} McCartney played [[Rhodes piano|Fender Rhodes electric piano]] on the track,{{sfn|Elson|1986|p=122}} while [[Denny Laine]] substituted for McCartney on bass guitar. The idea to tape the basic track and the orchestral arrangement simultaneously went against music industry convention, since the session musicians were paid by the hour.{{sfn|Rodriguez|2010|p=257}} Hewson recalled that he recruited "the best jazz musicians I knew ... They had this particular warm sound" and that the reason for the live recording was because McCartney wanted to capture "a certain feeling".{{sfn|Perasi|2013|p=87}} In music journalist Tom Breihan's description, although the song appears to lack a formal structure, "It chugs and twinkles with the slow confidence of an old [[torch song]], while the orchestra ... swells and contracts." According to Hewson, around 20 takes were performed over three hours, leaving the musicians tired and having to assure McCartney that their playing could not be improved on.{{sfn|Perasi|2013|p=87}} The song contains a guitar solo by [[Northern Irish]] guitarist [[Henry McCullough]],{{sfn|McGee|2003|pp=38–39}} who took the opportunity to express himself in his playing{{sfn|Rodriguez|2010|pp=257–58}} and depart from what he saw as McCartney's regimented approach to recording.{{sfn|Sounes|2010|p=302}} McCullough later said, "it had got to the point where I ''achingly'' wanted to be the guitar player in the band", rather than a sideman playing lines dictated by McCartney.{{sfn|Sounes|2010|p=302}} McCartney recalled in a 2010 interview:{{cite magazine|first=Tom|last=Doyle|title=Starting over (Paul McCartney: How I Survived ... the Beatles)|magazine=[[Mojo (magazine)|Mojo]]|date=October 2010|page=76}}
I'd sort of written the solo, as I often did write our solos. And he walked up to me right before the take and said, "Hey, would it be alright if I try something else?" And I said, "Er ... yeah." It was like, "Do I believe in this guy?" And he played the solo on "My Love", which came right out of the blue. And I just thought, Fucking great. And so there were plenty of moments like that where somebody's skill or feeling would overtake my wishes.{{cite web|first=Nick|last=Levine|title=Paul McCartney pays tribute to 'super-talented' Wings guitarist Henry McCullough|url=https://www.nme.com/news/music/wings-1199927|publisher=[[NME|nme.com]]|date=15 June 2016|access-date=17 July 2019|archive-date=17 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190717081904/https://www.nme.com/news/music/wings-1199927|url-status=live}}
According to McCullough, it was the first time anyone in Wings had challenged McCartney, and it was an approach that others in the band encouraged, in an effort to make Wings a genuine band and improve McCartney's image.{{sfn|McGee|2003|pp=161–62}} He described the result on "My Love" as "a stroke of luck, a gift from God really, and you get that in music".{{sfn|Doyle|2013|p=83}}{{refn|group=nb|In 2010, McCullough told ''[[The Irish News]]'' that he had drawn inspiration from "the power of the orchestra, the electric guitar slung round my neck and knowing that if I didn't come up with something I'd have to slink away with my head bowed".{{cite news|first=David|last=Roy|title=Funeral takes place of former Wings guitarist Henry McCullough|url=http://www.irishnews.com/news/2016/06/20/news/big-turnout-for-funeral-of-much-loved-music-man-mccullough-570140/|newspaper=[[The Irish News]]|date=19 June 2016|access-date=17 July 2019|archive-date=3 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190103223109/http://www.irishnews.com/news/2016/06/20/news/big-turnout-for-funeral-of-much-loved-music-man-mccullough-570140/|url-status=live}}}} In his book ''[[The Lyrics: 1956 to the Present]]'' (2021), McCartney called the solo "absolutely beautiful" and was proud he gave McCullough the freedom to improvise given his short tenure in the band at that point.{{sfn|McCartney|2021|pp=499–500}}

sections.heading: Release
Contemporary reviews
Retrospective assessments
sections.wikitext:
Writing in the 2004 edition of ''[[The Rolling Stone Album Guide]]'', [[Greg Kot]] described "My Love" as McCartney's "soggiest hit" and "over-orchestrated".{{sfn|Brackett|Hoard|2004|p=527}} Former ''[[Mojo (magazine)|Mojo]]'' editor [[Mat Snow]] calls it a "[[Slow dance|slow-dance]] single" that, although commercially successful, suffered unfavourable comparison with the Beatles' ''[[1962–1966]]'' and ''[[1967–1970]]'' compilation albums, which were released around the same time in 1973 and "reminded everyone of just how good Paul's old band was".{{sfn|Snow|2013|p=P-24}} Writing in 2017, ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' critic [[Rob Sheffield]] dismissed it as "the worst song any of the Beatles had anything to do with".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/05/04/books/review/rob-sheffield-dreaming-beatles.html|first=John|last=Williams|title=The Inexhaustible Four|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=4 May 2017|access-date=10 July 2019|archive-date=10 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190710072729/https://www.nytimes.com/2017/05/04/books/review/rob-sheffield-dreaming-beatles.html|url-status=live}}</ref> In Sheffield's opinion, McCartney was seeking to emulate the Beatles' 1969 ballad "[[Something (Beatles song)|Something]]", written by Harrison, but he missed the aesthetic significance of the six-note guitar "hook" that precedes the verse of Harrison's composition, instead inserting the "Wo-wo-wo-wo" refrain that sinks "My Love".{{sfn|Sheffield|2017|pp=208–09}} Sheffield says the ending provides a "whopper of unintentional comedy", as McCartney dramatically draws out the word "me" to become "''Meeeeeee-wo-wo-wo-wo-wo-ho, wo-ho, whooooa!''"{{sfn|Sheffield|2017|p=209}}{{refn|group=nb|This portion of the Wings recording was used in comedian [[Dickie Goodman]]'s 1973 single "Watergrate", a satire of the [[Watergate scandal]]. At the end of the song, Goodman asks Vice-President [[Spiro Agnew]] who will succeed [[Richard Nixon]] as US president, to which the answer comes as McCartney singing the final "me" from "My Love".{{sfn|Sheffield|2017|p=210}}}} In his song review for ''[[Stereogum]]'', Tom Breihan gives the track a score of five out of ten and concludes: "So 'My Love,' like a lot of McCartney songs, is a pretty and fluffy and sincere and meaningless thing – a song that would probably work as a prom ballad if it had the discipline to hit the big prom-ballad moments. It's nice enough, and I'll never understand, beyond simple name recognition, how it was as big as it was."<ref name="Breihan/Stereogum" />

Biographer [[Philip Norman (author)|Philip Norman]] pairs the song with "[[Maybe I'm Amazed]]" as "ode[s] to Linda" that, in the context of McCartney's songwriting in 1973, were "so far beyond his usual Wingspan that the dream-voices which had whispered "Yesterday" and "[[Let It Be (song)|Let It Be]]" into his ear might have returned".{{sfn|Norman|2016|p=463}} In his book on McCartney for the Praeger Singer-Songwriter Series, Vincent Benitez describes "My Love" as "an outstanding song highlighted by equally outstanding ensemble playing", particularly the "sublime solo" contributed by McCullough.{{sfn|Benitez|2010|p=43}} Robert Rodriguez, writing in his book on the Beatles' first decade as solo artists, says that McCullough's playing redeemed a "potentially mawkish McCartney valentine" and he considers the track to be the highlight of a mediocre album.{{sfn|Rodriguez|2010|pp=208, 258}} Former ''[[Record Collector]]'' editor [[Peter Doggett]] calls the song "sickly" and says that even after [[EMI]] had persuaded McCartney not to release ''Red Rose Speedway'' as a double LP, it remained an unimpressive collection of songs.{{sfn|Doggett|2011|p=208}}

sections.heading: Cover versions
sections.wikitext:
By the late 1970s, "My Love" was the second most-covered song written and released by a former Beatle since the band's break-up, after Harrison's "[[My Sweet Lord]]".{{sfn|Schaffner|1978|p=157}} [[Tony Bennett]], [[Nancy Wilson (jazz singer)|Nancy Wilson]] and [[Cass Elliot]] are among the many singers who recorded the song.{{sfn|Perasi|2013|p=87}} Others include [[Johnny Gill]], [[Cher]], [[Brenda Lee]] (from ''[[New Sunrise (Brenda Lee album)|New Sunrise]]''), [[Margie Joseph]], [[Salena Jones]], [[Mina Mazzini|Mina]], [[Shinehead]], [[Andy Williams]], [[Juice Newton]], [[Warren Hill (musician)|Warren Hill]], [[Dottie West]], and [[Mariah Carey]]. There have also been three jazz instrumental versions, by [[Ivan "Boogaloo Joe" Jones]], [[Pieces of a Dream (band)|Pieces of a Dream]] (from their 1996 album ''The Best of Pieces of a Dream''),<ref>{{cite web|url={{AllMusic|class=album|id=r1850842|pure_url=yes}}|title=The Best of Pieces of a Dream|work=[[AllMusic]]}}</ref> and [[Michael Lington]] (from the 2004 album ''Stay with Me'').<ref>{{cite web|url={{AllMusic|class=album|id=r690440|pure_url=yes}}|title=Stay with Me overview|work=[[AllMusic]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.allaboutjazz.com/php/review_print.php?id=14394|title=Stay with Me overview|work=[[All About Jazz]]|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041228135311/http://www.allaboutjazz.com/php/review_print.php?id=14394|archive-date=28 December 2004}}</ref>

An instrumental of the song can be heard during Monica and Chandler's wedding in the American sitcom ''[[Friends]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.paulmccartney.com/news-blogs/news/send-your-love-this-christmas-with-my-love|title=Send 'My Love' To Your Love!|publisher=PaulMcCartney.com|date=20 December 2018|access-date=18 July 2019|archive-date=6 November 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201106124725/https://www.paulmccartney.com/news-blogs/news/send-your-love-this-christmas-with-my-love|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Corinne Bailey Rae]] released a cover of the song on ''[[The Love EP (Corinne Bailey Rae EP)|The Love EP]]'' (2011).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/the-love-ep-mw0002083078 |title=Corinne Bailey Rae – The Love EP |publisher=[[AllMusic]] |access-date=1 March 2019 |archive-date=2 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190302210512/https://www.allmusic.com/album/the-love-ep-mw0002083078 |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Harry Connick Jr]] covered "My Love" on the 2014 album ''[[The Art of McCartney]]'', a tribute album to McCartney.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/the-art-of-mccartney-mw0002749491 |title=Various Artists – The Art of McCartney |publisher=[[AllMusic]] |access-date=7 December 2018 |archive-date=6 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180706104430/https://www.allmusic.com/album/the-art-of-mccartney-mw0002749491 |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2025, [[Mariah Carey]] covered the song for her album ''[[Here For It All]]''. ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' writer Heran Mamo noted that "while McCartney's original version is tender, Carey's is robust, her vocals overpowering the track's orchestration before giving way to the sentimental, reworked instrumental solo".<ref name="billboard1">{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/lists/mariah-carey-here-for-it-all-best-songs-ranked/mi/|title=Mariah Carey's 'Here for It All': All 11 Tracks Ranked|accessdate=September 27, 2025|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|date=September 25, 2025|last=Mamo|first=Heran}}</ref>
sections.text:
By the late 1970s, "My Love" was the second most-covered song written and released by a former Beatle since the band's break-up, after Harrison's "My Sweet Lord".{{sfn|Schaffner|1978|p=157}} Tony Bennett, Nancy Wilson and Cass Elliot are among the many singers who recorded the song.{{sfn|Perasi|2013|p=87}} Others include Johnny Gill, Cher, Brenda Lee (from New Sunrise), Margie Joseph, Salena Jones, Mina, Shinehead, Andy Williams, Juice Newton, Warren Hill, Dottie West, and Mariah Carey. There have also been three jazz instrumental versions, by Ivan "Boogaloo Joe" Jones, Pieces of a Dream (from their 1996 album The Best of Pieces of a Dream), and Michael Lington (from the 2004 album Stay with Me).

An instrumental of the song can be heard during Monica and Chandler's wedding in the American sitcom Friends. Corinne Bailey Rae released a cover of the song on The Love EP (2011). Harry Connick Jr covered "My Love" on the 2014 album The Art of McCartney, a tribute album to McCartney. In 2025, Mariah Carey covered the song for her album Here For It All. Billboard writer Heran Mamo noted that "while McCartney's original version is tender, Carey's is robust, her vocals overpowering the track's orchestration before giving way to the sentimental, reworked instrumental solo".
